LESSON: AREA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.2: Area
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do you work out area of different surfaces?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Collaboratively compare area of two surfaces directly by placing one surface on the other. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) during the discussion.

2. Team up with peers while using different unit square cut outs to cover a given surface. Those with poor motor coordination or missing limbs could use adapted

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Collaboratively compare area of two surfaces directly by placing one surface on the other. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) during the discussion.
2. Team up with peers while using different unit square cut outs to cover a given surface. Those with poor motor coordination or missing limbs could use adapted

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: learner works independently to calculate the area of squares and

rectangles by multiplying number of rows by the number of columns.

• Digital literacy: learner in pairs plays games involving area of rectangles and squares using digital

resources.

Values:
• Unity: learner works with peers harmoniously to establish that the area of a rectangle or a square is the

same as the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns.

• Integrity: learner gives honest answers while counting the number of unit square cutouts used to cover the

surface.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner counts the number of unit square cutouts prepared from locally available materials to cover the

surface to enhance environmental education.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate counting of the number of unit square cutouts prepared from locally available

resources to properties of matter in Science and Technology.
